title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Tracing and Controls for Compliance Teams
summary: A nine-module programme equipping compliance teams to detect crypto-asset financial crime, use blockchain analytics, meet travel rule and sanctions obligations, and investigate and report suspicion.
intro: This training programme equips compliance and financial crime teams at crypto-asset, payments and fintech firms to detect illicit flows, use blockchain analytics in monitoring, meet travel rule and sanctions obligations, and investigate and report suspicion.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give compliance, MLRO and financial crime teams a practical, firm-side command of crypto-asset financial crime: how criminals use the firm's services, how funds are traced on-chain, and what effective controls look like. Participants leave able to design and tune wallet screening and monitoring, handle travel rule and sanctions exposure, investigate alerts, file usable suspicion reports and respond to law enforcement, and evidence all of it to supervisors.
sections.What It Covers: The firm's crypto-asset financial crime exposure, typologies and red flags, the laundering lifecycle and anonymity-enhancing techniques, customer and wallet due diligence, blockchain analytics in transaction monitoring, the travel rule and counterparty due diligence, sanctions exposure, investigating alerts and suspicious activity reporting, and responding to law enforcement requests.
Intended Audience: MLROs, compliance officers and financial crime analysts at crypto-asset service providers
Financial crime teams at payment, e-money and fintech firms with crypto-asset exposure or crypto-asset business customers
Product, operations and risk managers responsible for onboarding, wallets, withdrawals and monitoring tools
Learning Objectives: Explain where crypto-asset financial crime risk enters the firm's business model, including indirect exposure through customers and partners
Identify the main typologies and red flags of crypto-enabled crime in customer behaviour and on-chain activity
Design customer, wallet and counterparty due diligence proportionate to the firm's risk
Apply blockchain analytics within transaction monitoring and sanctions controls, and recognise its limits
Investigate alerts, reach and document a judgement on suspicion, and file reports the national FIU can use
Respond effectively to law enforcement requests and evidence control effectiveness to supervisors
sections.Structure and Format: Nine modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a practitioner briefing with worked cases, red-flag and tracing exercises, ending in an alert-to-report workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT compliance or financial crime operations is helpful. No technical background in blockchain is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FATF, Virtual Assets Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (2020)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)

modules.title: The Firm's Crypto-Asset Financial Crime Exposure
modules.summary: Where financial crime risk enters crypto-asset, payment and fintech business models, what the FATF standards require of firms, and how to reflect crypto-asset exposure in the business-wide risk assessment.
objectives: Map financial crime risk across the firm's products, channels and fiat on- and off-ramps
Summarise the FATF obligations on virtual asset service providers and firms dealing with them
Reflect direct and indirect crypto-asset exposure in the business-wide risk assessment
syllabus: Exchanges, brokers, custodians, wallet providers and payment gateways: where risk arises
Indirect exposure: payment and e-money firms serving crypto-asset businesses
FATF Recommendations 15 and 16 and the risk-based approach for firms
Crypto-asset factors in the business-wide risk assessment and risk appetite

modules.title: Typologies and Red Flags for Compliance Teams
modules.summary: The principal ways criminals use crypto-asset services, from scams and ransomware to mule networks and sanctions evasion, and the customer and transaction red flags front-line and compliance staff should recognise.
objectives: Identify the main predicate offences and typologies involving crypto-assets
Recognise red flags in customer profiles, behaviour and transaction patterns
Translate typologies into monitoring scenarios and staff guidance
syllabus: Investment and romance scams, money mules and victims as unwitting launderers
Ransomware, darknet markets, hacks and cyber-enabled crime
Sanctions evasion, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
From red-flag indicators to scenarios, guidance and training

modules.title: The Laundering Lifecycle and Anonymity-Enhancing Techniques
modules.summary: How illicit proceeds are placed, layered and integrated using crypto-assets, how mixers, privacy coins, bridges and chain-hopping obscure the trail, and what the firm can still see and control.
objectives: Map placement, layering and integration to the firm's own services
Explain how mixers, privacy coins, bridges and decentralised protocols break transaction links
Set policy on anonymity-enhanced transfers and exposure to high-risk services
syllabus: Placement: cash-to-crypto, kiosks, peer-to-peer and over-the-counter trading
Layering: rapid hops, chain-hopping, bridges, swaps and decentralised protocols
Mixers, tumblers and privacy coins: what remains visible to the firm
Integration and off-ramps: where the firm is the exit point

modules.title: Customer and Wallet Due Diligence
modules.summary: How to onboard and keep under review customers whose activity involves crypto-assets, including source of funds and wealth, ownership of self-hosted wallets and risk-based enhanced due diligence.
objectives: Design a customer risk assessment that reflects crypto-asset activity
Verify source of funds and wealth derived from crypto-assets
Apply proportionate controls to self-hosted wallets and peer-to-peer transfers
syllabus: Customer risk factors for crypto-asset activity and business customers
Source of funds and wealth: using on-chain history as evidence
Self-hosted wallets: proof of ownership, risk scoring and limits
Enhanced due diligence, periodic review and trigger events

modules.title: Blockchain Analytics in Transaction Monitoring
modules.summary: How blockchain analytics tools trace funds, cluster and attribute addresses and score risk, and how to configure, tune and govern them within the firm's wider transaction monitoring framework.
objectives: Explain tracing, clustering and attribution in plain terms
Set exposure rules, thresholds and scenarios that fit the firm's risk
Govern analytics tools: selection, validation, coverage gaps and documentation
syllabus: Following funds on public ledgers: inputs, outputs and hops
Direct and indirect exposure, risk categories and scoring
Deposit and withdrawal screening, thresholds, tuning and false positives
Selecting, validating and overseeing an analytics provider

modules.title: The Travel Rule and Counterparty Due Diligence
modules.summary: How to implement the travel rule in practice, from collecting and transmitting originator and beneficiary information to due diligence on counterparty service providers and handling missing or inconsistent data.
objectives: Implement originator and beneficiary data requirements across transfer types
Conduct risk-based due diligence on counterparty service providers
Handle missing data, unhosted wallets and counterparties in jurisdictions without the rule
syllabus: FATF Recommendation 16 for virtual assets: data, timing and thresholds
Messaging solutions, interoperability and the uneven pace of adoption
Counterparty due diligence: licensing, controls and nested services
Missing or mismatched information: return, reject, review or report

modules.title: Sanctions Exposure in Crypto-Asset Activity
modules.summary: How sanctions risk arises through designated addresses, sanctioned services and jurisdictions, and how the firm screens, blocks, freezes and reports in a twenty-four-hour, borderless market.
objectives: Identify direct and indirect sanctions exposure in on-chain and customer activity
Design address, customer and geolocation screening controls
Respond to a sanctions hit: freezing, holding and reporting to the authority
syllabus: Designated addresses, sanctioned services and high-risk jurisdictions
Address screening, IP and device geolocation and evasion indicators
Exposure through counterparties, nested exchanges and decentralised protocols
Freezing, holding and reporting crypto-assets and handling tainted deposits

modules.title: Investigating Alerts and Reporting Suspicion
modules.summary: How to triage and investigate on-chain and customer alerts, reach and record a reasoned judgement on suspicion, and write reports that the national FIU and law enforcement can act on.
objectives: Run a structured investigation combining on-chain and off-chain information
Reach and document a defensible decision on suspicion
Write suspicious activity reports with usable crypto-asset detail
syllabus: Alert triage, escalation and case management
Investigation steps: customer profile, tracing, counterparties and open sources
Decision records, tipping off and restricting or exiting relationships
Report quality: addresses, transaction hashes, attribution and narrative

modules.title: Responding to Law Enforcement and Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining how the firm handles production orders, freezing requests and asset recovery, ending with a workshop that takes a case from alert to report and law enforcement response.
objectives: Handle information requests, production orders and freezing requests correctly
Support seizure and return of crypto-assets while protecting the firm
Apply the programme to a realistic case and agree control improvements
syllabus: Verifying, prioritising and responding to law enforcement requests
Freezing, preserving and transferring assets: keys, custody and records
Public-private partnerships and evidencing effectiveness to supervisors
Workshop: from alert to report, response and control remediation

related.title: Financial Crime Compliance in the Age of AI
related.summary: A ten-module programme for MLROs and financial crime teams on the risk-based approach, AI-driven detection, AI-enabled threats and evidencing effectiveness to supervisors.

related.title: Fraud and Scams: Prevention, Detection and Response
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on preventing, detecting and responding to fraud and scams, from authorised push payment scams and deepfakes to reimbursement and board reporting.

related.title: MLRO and Financial Crime Leadership
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving MLROs and deputies the tools to lead the firm's financial crime framework, report to the board and handle supervisory inspections.

related.title: Sanctions Compliance
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on designing and running effective sanctions compliance, from ownership and screening to evasion typologies, licensing and breach reporting.

related.title: The EU AML Package: AMLR, AMLD6 and AMLA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AML package for supervisors and firms: the AML Regulation single rulebook, AMLD6, AMLA's supervisory model, crypto-asset transfers and transition planning.

related.title: Compliance Officer Academy
related.summary: A ten-module academy giving compliance officers the tools to run an independent, risk-based compliance function and handle supervisory engagement with confidence.
